summary: Spent 5 of 6 runs on model-size scaling (DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO/HEAD_DIM/GQA) around the baseline (DEPTH=8, dim=512, val_bpb=0.997333); every variant was worse than or at best on par with baseline, showing the baseline architecture is a well-tuned local optimum on that axis. The shared results.tsv showed other commits combining a halved TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE (2^18) with EMBEDDING_LR=0.8 reaching 0.988312, so my final run applied that combo plus my own addition (WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->0.3, motivated by the extra optimizer steps from the smaller batch), giving val_bpb=0.990769 -- clearly better than baseline and my own prior best, though the extra warmdown shortening did not clearly beat the 0.988312 reference (plausibly noise). Next step: isolate whether batch-size or embedding-LR is doing the work by testing each alone at this model size, and try the batch/LR combo without any warmdown change as the cleanest replication.
